### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.sessions

### Neovim version

0.12 (!at least latest Nightly build!)

### Description

I have the following opts:
```lua
opts = {
    autoread = false,
    directory = vim.fn.stdpath 'data' .. '/sessions',
    file = '', -- File for local session (use `''` to disable)
    hooks = {
      pre = {
        read = function()
          vim.cmd [[ exec 'silent! bufdo w' ]]
        end,
      },
      post = {
        read = function()
          if vim.fn.mode() == 'i' then
            vim.cmd [[ stopinsert ]]
          end
        end,
      },
    },
  }
```
I wrote it when I got an error trying to save a session with unsaved buffers. I expected to work but could not figure out why the behaviour never changed, regardless of what version of saving all buffers I tried, even async calls. Then I gd'd into the read() fn and saw that it executes the pre hooks after checking for unsaved buffers and throwing an error when it finds them. 

This was unexpected and unintuitive behaviour. Pre-hooks, I think, are supposed to allow us to configure how we deal with problems like unsaved buffers, however we choose and this got in the way of that.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Replace this with description of interactive reproduction steps along with the behavior you observe.
   Feel free to include images/videos/etc, this helps a lot.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

This is a documented behavior: `pre` hooks [run before *successful* action](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/94cae4660a8b2d95dbbd56e1fbc6fcfa2716d152/doc/mini-sessions.txt#L99), at least what can be reasonably expected to be a successful action. Having unsaved buffer(s) is considered harmful for `read()` (as all buffers will be wiped out and unsaved data will be lost), so it is verified first before performing a `read()`.

There are several choices to overcome unsaved buffers before `read()`:
- Write custom wrapper that first saves all buffers. Something like this:

    ```lua
    _G.my_session_read = function(...)
      vim.cmd('silent! bufdo write')
      MiniSessions.read(...)
    end
    ```

    The same can be done for `MiniSessions.select('read')`.

- Use `{ force = true }` to ignore unsaved buffers (data will be lost).

As I think that autosaving buffers is generally not the best practice (as saving should require user attention) but *there is* a way to do that, I am going to close this as expected behavior (which intentionally introduces friction for this use case).

title: Run pre hooks before checking for unsaved buffers in MiniSession.read()
